evals.prompt: i'm getting `Error: While lock file: ./pear/app-storage/.../db/LOCK: Resource temporarily unavailable` every time my app starts. i didn't change anything. help
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses two-Corestores-on-same-store OR two processes against the same store. Fix: one Corestore per app, use store.namespace() to subdivide; check ps aux for stale processes.

evals.prompt: writer is appending blocks but my reader process never sees the new ones. i call core.get(latestIndex) and it hangs
evals.expected_output: Reader must `await core.update()` to learn about new metadata. Also remind to await core.ready() before reading .key/.length.

evals.prompt: i want a key-value store inside my pear app that syncs to peers. should i build it on hypercore or hyperbee?
evals.expected_output: Hyperbee — ordered K/V on a core with batches and range queries. Sample with keyEncoding/valueEncoding.

evals.prompt: i have a primary core. how do i tell a new peer about the keys of three secondary cores so they can read them too?
evals.expected_output: Bootstrap pattern: write the secondary keys into the first block of the primary core; reader fetches primary, parses block 0, then store.get({key}) for each.

assertions.value: Explains that Corestore replication does NOT carry keys and that they must be exchanged either in-band (primary core) or out-of-band.

evals.prompt: show me the smallest correct example of replicating one hypercore between two peers (writer and reader)
evals.expected_output: Writer: store, core, append, swarm.join(discoveryKey), swarm.on('connection', conn => store.replicate(conn)). Reader: store.get({key}), await ready, swarm.join(discoveryKey), await update, then get blocks. Pear.teardown for swarm.destroy.
